summary: Frontend-only test pass (no backend exists) for the new Studio Design tab, editable Code tab, Content tab rewrite and localStorage cross-page sync. Verified via Playwright on the public preview URL. Core feature logic works: framer-motion drag, all style inspector props, layer reorder, code<->elements two-way sync, content single-source-of-truth, cross-tab state retention, localStorage -> /preview '03' variation. Two defects found: (1) CRITICAL layout bug that makes most canvas blocks un-clickable / un-draggable (canvas overflows its column to the left because of justify-content:center), (2) Code tab text is not regenerated on accent change and a subsequent code edit bakes the stale effective background into every element's bg, permanently breaking accent inheritance. No console errors or page errors observed anywhere, incl. during drag and rapid tab switching.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: .design-canvas is a fixed 760x420 with flex-shrink:0 inside .design-canvas-wrap{display:flex;justify-content:center;overflow:auto}, but the grid column is only ~317px (desktop 1920) / ~316px (mobile 390). Centering pushes the canvas ~220px OUTSIDE the wrap on the LEFT, which is unreachable (scrollLeft cannot be negative) and renders behind sibling columns. Measured desktop: wrap left=958, canvas left=737. Consequence: document.elementFromPoint at design-block-cta centre returns design-layers-list and at design-block-image centre returns design-content-input; Playwright normal click on design-block-cta times out with '.design-layers intercepts pointer events'. So the CTA and Image blocks cannot be selected or dragged at all, and headline/subtext are only draggable from their right-hand visible portion. Fix: justify-content:flex-start (overflow then scrollable), and/or scale/responsive canvas, and/or give the canvas its own full-width row.

codeText is only regenerated on element update / done-transition, not when the accent colour changes, so the Code tab shows a stale background (e.g. accent set to #ff00ff but code still shows background: "#3b82f6" for the CTA).

integration_issues.flow: Accent colour inheritance after a Code-tab edit
integration_issues.issue: generateCode() writes the EFFECTIVE background into the code and parseCodeToElements() writes it back as an explicit el.bg override. After any code edit, elements become {headline:'transparent', subtext:'transparent', cta:'#3b82f6', image:'#e5e5e0'}, so later accent changes no longer affect the CTA in the canvas, Live Preview iframe or /preview, and 'Reset to accent' now appears for every element (text blocks get an explicit 'transparent' bg). Repro: Done -> Code tab -> change 'top: 224' to 'top: 260' -> change accent to #00aa00 -> CTA stays #3b82f6. Suggested fix: emit/parse a sentinel (or skip writing bg back when the parsed value equals the effective accent/default).

issues: Canvas blocks are visually clipped mid-word and bleed over/under the layers column and inspector because of the negative-left overflow (see ui_bugs #1); at 390px the canvas left edge sits at -185px so the headline/subtext/CTA left edges are permanently invisible.
No page-level horizontal overflow at 390px (mobile stacking works).

action_items: Fix .design-canvas-wrap centering/overflow so the whole 760px canvas is reachable (justify-content:flex-start + scroll, or scale the canvas, or full-width canvas row). Currently CTA + Image blocks are undraggable/unselectable.
Regenerate codeText when accent changes, and stop parseCodeToElements from converting inherited/effective backgrounds into explicit el.bg overrides (breaks accent inheritance permanently).
critical_code_review_comments: studio.css .design-canvas-wrap uses justify-content:center with an oversized fixed-width child - always produces unreachable left overflow inside an overflow:auto container.

mock.js generateCode/parseCodeToElements round-trip is lossy: effective bg (accent/default) is written back as an explicit override; consider emitting `background: "accent"`/omitting it for inherited values.

Studio.jsx: setCodeText is called inside the setElements updater (side effect in a reducer) - works today but is unsafe under StrictMode double-invocation; move it to a useEffect on [elements, accent] which also fixes the stale-accent code issue.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (9/11 scenarios fully pass; drag partially blocked, accent-after-code-edit fails)

seed_data_creation: None (client-side mock only; localStorage key framewright.studio-design was cleared/repopulated during tests)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified PASS: /generate -> dev-state-done -> 4 tabs; layers list (4 rows, up/down swap works, first-up & last-down disabled); style inspector (fontSize/weight/color/bg/width/padding/align all reflected live in live-preview-iframe style attr); design-bg-reset appears/clears correctly; framer-motion drag works with real mouse.down/move/up when the grab point is inside the wrap's VISIBLE area (delta +80/+60 applied and clamped in-bounds) - use a point near the block's right edge, not its centre, until the canvas overflow bug is fixed; editable Code tab two-way sync (top:224->300 moved canvas block and iframe; renaming CTA text propagated); pipeline-code-copy-button works; Content tab dropdown+textarea is single source of truth (edit shows up in design-content-input and the iframe); tab cycling loses no state; /preview shows 01/02/03 with custom-preview-iframe matching Studio edits after nav from Studio; smoke: 5 dev states, generate ~3.4s -> DONE, Home/Studio/Preview nav no blank flicker, 390px no horizontal overflow. Not retested: mock login/logout, job history (covered in iterations 4/5).
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the undraggable blocks: .design-canvas (760px, flex-shrink:0) is centered inside a ~317px .design-canvas-wrap with overflow:auto. Flexbox centering distributes the 443px overflow to both sides; the left half becomes unreachable/negative scroll space and is painted outside the wrap, where sibling grid columns (.design-layers, .design-inspector) sit above it in paint order and swallow pointer events. Any block whose visible centre falls in that region (CTA, Image) cannot receive pointerdown, so neither selection nor framer-motion drag can start.
